app.title: Functional Scoliosis Assessment
app.summary: The person first confirms the recording setup in a sidebar checklist, which warns when conditions differ from the protocol. They then either point the tool at a folder of subjects or enter one subject's demographics and upload their standing, walking and optional sitting trial files of tracked joint positions. Running the pipeline smooths each trial, computes left and right shoulder and hip angles frame by frame, and averages them across repeated trials for each phase. It shows a demographics table, per-phase angle tables, a written inference that places each subject in an asymmetry band, and time-domain and STFT plots of the walking signals. It also writes all of these to an output folder as CSV, PNG, JSON and text files.

task.text: Turn repeated trials of tracked skeleton joints into per-subject shoulder and hip asymmetry tables, frequency plots and a screening-style inference, so subjects can be compared between standing and walking.

data.text: Per-subject folders, each with a demographics record and several trial files. Each trial file is a timestamped sequence of 3D joint positions from a depth camera, an RGB pose estimator or an offline dump, grouped into protocol phases.
data.item: one trial of tracked joint positions for a subject in one phase (static standing, dynamic walking or optional sitting)

stage.text: analysing recorded posture and gait trials after capture, before writing up the comparison

mechanism.text: A sidebar checklist and backend choice frame the run. Two tabs then take either a whole dataset folder or one subject's form and uploaded files, and a run button computes everything at once. The results appear below as tables, an inference text block and paired four-panel time-domain and STFT figures, and the same files are written to disk.

field.text: markerless motion-capture assessment of postural and gait asymmetry in clinical biomechanics

workflow.name: compute summary measures per subject across repeated trials and export a report pack

steps.step: check the recording conditions against the protocol
steps.here: The sidebar asks for the camera distance, clothing, room lighting, camera height and an optional treadmill speed, and shows a warning for each condition that departs from the protocol.
Either generate sample subjects and name a dataset folder of subject_* folders, or fill in one subject's demographics and upload static, dynamic and optional sitting trial files in JSON or CSV.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: 'Run study pipeline' or 'Build report from uploaded trials' smooths the joints and computes the angle at each shoulder and hip, plus the left−right differences. These are averaged per trial and then across the trials of each phase.

The static and dynamic tables place every subject's shoulder and hip angles next to each other. The inference text gives each subject an asymmetry band and the dynamic−static change, and ranks subjects by dynamic shoulder deviation.

steps.step: look at the signal over time and in frequency
steps.here: Four-panel time-domain plots of the right and left shoulder and hip angles sit beside four-panel STFT spectrograms, with a note saying why the FFT is not used for the interpretation.
Writes CSV tables for demographics, static, dynamic and sitting phases, the inference text, session and dataset JSON, and PNG plots to the output folder.

distinctive: A setup checklist turns departures from the capture protocol (distance, clothing, lighting, camera height) into visible warnings before any analysis.
Trials are grouped into protocol phases (static standing, dynamic walking, optional sitting), and repeated trials are averaged within each phase so static and dynamic values can be contrasted.
The measure is a left−right angle difference at the shoulders and at the hips, computed from a fixed set of skeleton joints after Kinect-style smoothing.
Data from several capture sources (depth cameras, an RGB pose model, offline dumps) is normalised to one joint schema, so the metrics do not depend on the camera.
The written inference assigns heuristic asymmetry bands and states explicitly that it is a research aid, not a diagnosis.
